question: Which of the following best describes the species coverage of Indian polyvalent anti-snake venom (ASV)?

answers.text: It covers only haematotoxic species (Russell's viper and saw-scaled viper) and must be combined with a separate neurotoxic antivenom for elapid bites

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Indian polyvalent ASV is formulated to cover all four medically significant species — both haematotoxic (Russell's viper, saw-scaled viper) AND neurotoxic (spectacled cobra, common krait). A separate elapid-specific product is not required.

answers.text: It covers all four Big Four species — Russell's viper, saw-scaled viper, spectacled cobra, and common krait — providing both haematotoxic and neurotoxic venom neutralisation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Indian polyvalent ASV is raised by immunising horses with venom from all four Big Four species and neutralises both haematotoxic (viper) and neurotoxic (elapid) venoms. The same vial is used regardless of whether the envenomation is haematotoxic or neurotoxic.

answers.text: It covers only cobras and kraits; a separate viper antivenom must be ordered for Russell's viper or saw-scaled viper bites

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Indian polyvalent ASV covers all four Big Four species including both vipers (Russell's and saw-scaled) and elapids (cobra and krait). A separate viper-only product does not need to be ordered.

answers.text: Coverage depends on the manufacturer; some brands cover only three of the four Big Four species

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect for practical purposes. The standard Indian polyvalent ASV available in government and district hospitals is formulated against all four Big Four species. Students should know this as the standard polyvalent product.

overallFeedback.feedback: Indian polyvalent ASV covers ALL four Big Four species: Russell's viper + saw-scaled viper (haematotoxic) AND spectacled cobra + common krait (neurotoxic). One product for all four — no species-specific product needed in practice.
Correct. One polyvalent product covers all four Big Four species — both haematotoxic and neurotoxic. Same vial regardless of species.
